A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RelationField, with matching authors and readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and six-page supplements. Content can be matched across appendix reordering and figure relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original 3DSSG scene-graph results, ScanNet++ relationship-guided segmentation results, and ablations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 5–8.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a LangSplat comparison and empirical Gaussian Splatting results.

M1.justification: v1 Appendix F sketches a future Gaussian Splatting adaptation. v2 Appendix E implements this extension using pairs of Gaussian centers and initialization from a NeRF-exported point cloud. The core NeRF architecture, supervision, loss, and querying procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain relationship querying on LERF, ScanNet++, and Replica scenes, scene-graph prediction on RIO10/3DSSG, and relationship-guided segmentation on ScanNet++. The additions vary the comparator and scene representation without introducing a distinct task or data domain.

E2.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 2 add LangSplat alongside LERF and OpenNeRF. LangSplat was previously cited but not evaluated in this comparison. Table 1 retains the same scene-graph baselines.

E3.justification: New Figure 11 introduces a NeRF-versus-Gaussian-Splatting rendering comparison reporting FPS and memory. The existing recall, IoU, and accuracy evaluations, eight-scene segmentation benchmark, and 30,000-step NeRF training schedule remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E and new Figure 11 test whether Gaussian Splatting preserves relationship responses while changing rendering efficiency. The existing 3D-consistency, language-model, text-encoder, and relationship-direction analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new FPS and memory averages do not specify an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds LangSplat at 0.49 IoU and 0.87 accuracy; RelationField remains at 0.53 and 0.96. New Figure 11 reports approximately 1.7 versus 7.1 FPS and 22 versus 26 GB for NeRF versus Gaussian Splatting. Existing Table 1 and Figure 6 values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), the feature definitions, cosine-similarity loss, and query-scoring formulation are unchanged. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs, and the Gaussian Splatting extension adds no formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal claims about relationship-aware radiance fields, state-of-the-art scene graphs, and the new segmentation task retain their meaning. The introductory contribution bullets are consolidated, while the Gaussian Splatting experiment supports representation-independence already asserted in v1.

C2.justification: v2 attributes faster convergence and improved memory utilization to NeRF-based Gaussian initialization and interprets Figure 11 as supporting geometry independence. Its additional claim of a lower Gaussian Splatting memory footprint conflicts with the figure's 26 GB versus 22 GB. Section 5's limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly quantifies the existing dictionary-based feature-storage scheme at approximately 500 MB per scene in FP16. Appendix E documents Gaussian initialization, and Figure 11 reports approximately 1.1 million Gaussians. Existing training hardware, budgets, and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lee et al., Rethinking Open-Vocabulary Segmentation of Radiance Fields in 3D Space, as the source for Gaussian initialization. LangSplat gains an evaluated-comparator role, but was already cited in v1. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Edits consolidate the first two contribution bullets, expand the Gaussian Splatting discussion, swap Appendices E and F, and remove the corresponding future-work sentence from the conclusion. Other changes are localized wording corrections and an added funding acknowledgement.

P2.justification: v2 adds the Gaussian Splatting comparison as Figure 11 and a LangSplat row to Table 2. Figure 3 moves, retained appendix figures are reordered, and the original Figure 11 becomes Figure 13. Existing visual content is otherwise retained with resizing and page-flow adjustments.

improvement.justification: The added LangSplat baseline strengthens the central segmentation comparison, and the Gaussian Splatting demonstration supplies evidence for an extension previously left as future work. These provide a limited net improvement alongside useful implementation details. The efficiency conclusion requires caution: Appendix E claims lower memory use, but Figure 11 reports 26 GB for Gaussian Splatting versus 22 GB for NeRF.
